key_insight: WorldGuide turns video generation into a goal-directed control loop: it can decide the next action from the state it has already generated, execute that action, and keep going until the task is done. This makes video world models more useful for long-horizon procedural tasks than open-loop generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between plausible video synthesis and reliable task execution. Existing approaches either generate videos without adapting to what actually happened, or depend on external executors and indirect checks instead of closing the loop within the model itself.
method: Uses a goal-directed video world model that conditions each next step on the generated state so far.
Predicts the next action, simulates or executes it, and updates the rollout based on the observed outcome.
Includes a completion-aware mechanism so the model can recognize when the procedural task is finished.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward video models that are not just realistic but also actionable and task-aware. It can improve planning, robotics-like procedural execution, and interactive agent systems that need to adapt over long horizons.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing state -> action prediction -> execution -> updated state -> completion check.
Side-by-side comparison of open-loop generation versus closed-loop goal-directed generation.
A timeline graphic illustrating long-horizon task execution with feedback at each step.
Icons for goal, action, feedback, and completion to highlight the control loop.
paper_title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
paper_authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Hisham Cholakkal, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan
